name: copy_block_backward_then_jump
description: Copies a block of bytes from a source to a destination, working from the end backward, then transfers control through a jump table that was not recovered. The facts also list a COLOR00 register write, library open calls and startup error text.

name: open_library_and_measure_text
description: Opens a library through the system library table, measures a text string up to its terminator, and then makes two further library calls. The text itself is not written out in the pseudo-code shown, so its use is not confirmed.

name: scan_memory_regions_by_type
description: Loops over 32 memory regions and probes up to 256 sample addresses in each through the exec memory-type call. A region that reports a match adds to a running total and sets or clears bits in two masks, one of which depends on a type flag, and the results go to globals.

name: allocate_memory_via_exec
description: Calls the exec memory allocation routine along with three other library offsets, with one caller and one callee. The decompiler timed out, so the description rests only on the instruction count and these calls.

name: set_flag_on_signature_match

name: set_global_to_fifteen
description: Stores fifteen into a global variable and returns immediately. The facts list a COLOR00 register access that the short pseudo-code does not show, so that access is not described here.

name: copy_block_and_relocate_code
description: Copies a block of long words backward, in groups of eight, from a source area to a destination computed from globals. It then copies a fixed run of its own following code words to a second location, and the facts list two calls to unnamed routines.

key: Cannon Fodder (1993)(Virgin)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 3).adf boot-block load +$400 to $040000 (9216 bytes):0:007C
name: copy_counted_byte_runs
description: Reads word counts from calls to other routines and copies that many bytes from a source to a destination in nested loops. When the loops end it copies eleven words from a global table onto the stack and makes an indirect call that was not recovered.

key: Cannon Fodder (1993)(Virgin)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 3).adf boot-block load +$400 to $040000 (9216 bytes):0:00AC
name: copy_byte_runs_until_done
description: Copies a run of bytes, then repeatedly reads a count and copies further byte runs until a 16-bit counter runs out. At the end it copies eleven words from a global table onto the stack and makes an indirect call that was not recovered.

key: Cannon Fodder (1993)(Virgin)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 3).adf boot-block load +$400 to $040000 (9216 bytes):0:00F6
name: extract_flag_bit_from_table
description: Scans a table of word pairs until a masked word matches the second word of a pair, then reads a shift count from that table entry and extracts one bit from a masked word. It calls another routine when a signed byte comparison overflows, and returns the resulting value.

key: Cannon Fodder (1993)(Virgin)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 3).adf boot-block load +$400 to $040000 (9216 bytes):0:0130
name: mask_and_conditional_call
description: Bitwise ANDs one word with another, and when one byte value is below another it calls a further routine and returns that routine's word instead of the masked value.

name: accumulate_32bit_from_bytes
description: Reads four consecutive bytes from the address held in a register and shifts each one into a 32-bit result, which is returned. The pointer register advances after each byte.

key: Cannon Fodder (1993)(Virgin)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 3).adf boot-block load +$400 to $040000 (9216 bytes):0:0160
name: build_bit_code_table
description: Reads a count and fills a stack buffer with that many bytes via another routine. For each code length from one to sixteen it assigns bit-reversed codes to matching entries and stores masks and lengths in a table.

key: Cannon Fodder (1993)(Virgin)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 3).adf boot-block load +$400 to $040000 (9216 bytes):0:01E8
name: copy_table_to_stack_jump
description: Copies eleven words from a global table onto the stack, working backward, then makes an indirect call whose target was not recovered. It has one caller.

name: set_global_to_ten
description: Stores ten into a global variable and returns. The decompiler shows only those two instructions, so nothing more is described.

name: enter_infinite_loop
description: Loops forever without performing any operation, so it never returns. The facts list four instructions and an execution in the reference run, and nothing else is shown.

name: run_conditional_call_sequence
description: Tests a global variable and, when a condition holds, updates it and runs a long series of calls to other routines. On one failing branch it sets the global to minus one. The facts list two unnamed routine calls.

name: check_threshold_with_no_effect
description: Contains a conditional block that subtracts a value from itself twice, which leaves the variables unchanged, then copies globals onto themselves. The condition needs a variable to be zero and above a threshold at once, so the block cannot change anything.

name: calculate_and_store_offsets
description: Reads a value from a global and a lookup table, triples it, and stores that value plus three fixed offsets into a set of word-sized global buffers. A second branch recomputes the offsets from doubled values when a global is zero.

name: copy_block_then_clear_globals
description: Copies a long-word block of about ten thousand entries from one fixed area to another, then clears ten global variables. The facts list only the instruction count and no calls.

name: modify_global_on_condition
description: Calls another routine and then adjusts a global variable. Depending on its value it calls a further routine, or it inverts the variable for one pair of values or sets it to all ones for another.

name: write_ciaa_interrupt_control
description: Stores a routine address into one global and a fixed control value, with bits seven and three set, into another, which the facts tie to the CIAA interrupt control register. The routine then returns.

name: set_state_and_call_update
description: Sets a global variable to four, calls another routine to update state, and returns the register pair unchanged. The facts list the INTREQ interrupt request register, which the short pseudo-code does not show.

name: enter_infinite_loop
description: Enters an endless loop that performs no operations, so it never returns. The facts also list interrupt, timer and keyboard serial registers, but the pseudo-code makes none of those accesses.

name: read_table_byte_as_index
description: Reads a byte from a table, indexed by a global variable, and stores it back there, setting the top bit when the value is a particular code. It then zeroes the variable.

name: compute_clamped_mouse_movement
description: Calls another routine and, when a flag is zero, computes a movement value from differences between two stored counters, shifts and doubles it, then clamps it to a fixed minimum and maximum. The facts list the JOY0DAT mouse movement register.

name: read_fire_button_state
description: Reads bits of the CIAA port A register and the pot input register to set two global flags for button presses. Each flag becomes all ones when its bit is clear and zero otherwise.

name: clear_color_tables
description: Writes zero into sixteen words of memory, then into thirty-two consecutive hardware color registers starting at the COLOR01 register. The facts list only COLOR01, so the color range is inferred from the addresses.

name: fade_palette_colors
description: When a flag is zero, clamps a level between zero and fifteen and darkens sixteen packed color words by subtracting it from each four-bit channel, clamped at zero. Otherwise it runs a call sequence, copies sixteen words and sets several globals.

name: call_with_global_cleared
description: Saves a global variable, zeroes it, calls another routine, then restores the saved value. The facts list one call to an unnamed routine.

name: fade_palette_with_stride
description: When a flag is zero, clamps a level between zero and fifteen and darkens sixteen packed color words by subtracting it from each four-bit channel, writing them with a variable stride. Otherwise it runs a call sequence, copies sixteen words and sets several globals.

name: run_sequence_and_copy_palette
description: Runs a fixed sequence of calls to other routines, copies sixteen words from one buffer to another, then sets several globals before calling more routines. The facts list seven unnamed calls.

name: run_loop_until_flag_set
description: Stores its argument in a global, calls two routines, then loops over a counter calling another routine until a global becomes non-zero. It finishes by setting two more globals and returns.

name: shift_palette_buffers
description: Calls routines to set globals, then walks sixteen words at a time, copying one buffer into a second and moving words from a third buffer into the first. It finishes with another call.

name: poll_routine_until_zero
description: Repeatedly calls another routine until it returns zero, then sets a global variable to two and makes one more call. The facts list one unnamed routine call.

name: process_pointer_list_entries
description: Walks a table of pointers until an end marker. For each entry it either records a fixed value or copies sixteen words from a source block, then skips a run of bytes ended by a negative marker, updating globals and calling routines along the way. The facts also reference a text string naming a RAW file.

name: call_two_routines_in_order
description: Calls two other routines in sequence and returns. The pseudo-code contains nothing else, so no further behaviour is described.

name: copy_split_word_buffers
description: Copies sixteen words from a source table into two destination buffers, with the first fed from the upper half of the source and the second from the lower half. The facts list two callers.

name: copy_split_word_buffers
description: Copies sixteen words from a source buffer into two destinations, with one destination fed from the upper half of the source and the other from the lower half. The facts list only the instruction count and that the routine is unreached.

name: run_sixteen_step_call_loop
description: Calls one routine, resets a counter, then runs a loop of sixteen steps. Each step calls five routines and one more when a flag is set, and the counter advances by two per step.

name: run_loop_while_counter_nonzero
description: Sets a global counter to fifteen, calls a routine, then loops calling two routines until a doubled copy of the counter becomes zero, and returns zero. The facts list four callers.

name: decrement_counter_twice_and_call
description: Decrements a global variable by one twice, but only when it is non-zero, then calls two other routines. The facts list one caller.

name: clear_global_byte_block
description: Writes zero to seven global variables and returns. The facts list two callers.

name: rotate_buffers_from_source
description: Stores the previous contents of one twelve-word buffer into a second buffer while loading new words from a caller-supplied source into the first. It then moves twenty-four words between a third buffer and a global block. The facts list one caller.

name: copy_two_word_blocks
description: Copies twelve words from one buffer into another, then copies twenty-four words from a second source into a third destination. The facts list two callers.

name: advance_pointer_and_rotate_value
description: Sets a flag bit in a byte just before an input address, then advances a stored pointer by four and wraps it to a fixed start when it passes a limit. It combines two values read through that pointer and a global, and stores the result rotated.

name: increment_byte_counters
description: When a global counter is non-zero and a multiple of four, increments four byte counters that are below the at-sign character. It calls another routine when the counter is non-zero, and a further routine when the counter is a multiple of sixty-four.

name: decrement_byte_counters
description: Decrements each of four byte variables by one when it is not zero. The facts list one caller.

name: dispatch_four_byte_slots
description: When a global is non-zero, derives a two-bit phase value from a byte and toggles a flag when it wraps. It then passes four stored byte values one at a time to a called routine with their index and returns the last result from that routine. The facts list the first custom chip register.

name: run_conditional_routine_block
description: Tests two flag fields in a structure and a byte in another. When both conditions hold it runs a fixed set of routine calls and returns; otherwise, when a different pair of fields is set, it calls five other routines.

name: write_entry_if_flagged
description: Reads a flag byte at a fixed offset in a structure, clears its lowest bit, and when that bit was set writes a computed word and a copied word through a pointer stored in the structure. The facts list only the instruction count and one caller.

name: check_flag_and_set_status
description: Reads a flag byte in a structure and clears its lowest bit. When the bit was set it fills a neighbouring byte with all ones and stores a word from another field, with fixed high bits set, into a second structure.

name: copy_word_between_structures
description: Copies one word from a fixed offset in an input structure to a fixed offset in a second structure. The facts list only four instructions and that the routine is unreached.

name: dispatch_script_opcode_stream
description: Reads opcodes from a script data stream and dispatches each one. Most store bytes or words into object fields, and some call further routines, while two countdown fields are decremented on each pass. The facts list two unnamed calls and four callers.

name: enter_script_opcode_dispatch
description: Single-instruction entry into the shared script opcode dispatcher, which reads a byte from a stream and branches on it. The facts show one caller and one unnamed call, and nothing else is listed.

name: enter_script_opcode_dispatch
description: Single-instruction entry into the shared script opcode dispatcher, which reads a byte from a stream and branches on it. The facts show one unnamed call and no registers or text.

name: enter_script_opcode_dispatch
description: Single-instruction entry into the shared script opcode dispatcher, which reads a byte from a stream and branches on it. The facts show one caller and one unnamed call.

name: enter_script_opcode_dispatch
description: Single-instruction entry into the shared script opcode dispatcher, which reads a byte from a stream and branches on it. The facts show one caller and one unnamed call.

name: enter_script_opcode_dispatch
description: Single-instruction entry into the shared script opcode dispatcher, which reads a byte from a stream and branches on it. The routine is unreached according to the facts, and it makes one unnamed call.

name: enter_script_opcode_dispatch
description: Single-instruction entry into the shared script opcode dispatcher, which reads a byte from a stream and branches on it. The facts show one unnamed call and no other registers or text.

name: dispatch_script_opcode_stream
description: Shared script dispatcher with ten instructions, reading bytes from a stream and branching on each opcode to store values into object fields or call routines. The facts show three callers and three unnamed calls.

name: dispatch_script_opcode_stream
description: Shared script dispatcher with thirty-three instructions, reading bytes from a stream and branching on each opcode to store values into object fields or call routines. The facts show two callers and one unnamed call.

name: run_three_update_routines
description: Calls three other routines in sequence and returns. The facts list one caller, and the pseudo-code contains nothing else.

name: scale_and_clamp_value
description: Multiplies two stored words, scales the product down by shifts and by a further word, and stores it in a structure field. Values above sixty-four are clamped to sixty-four before the result is stored in a second field.

name: advance_envelope_index_and_scale
description: When a table pointer is set, adds a scaled table byte to a 16-bit value, then advances an index through the table. The index wraps to twice a stored start value when it reaches a limit. The facts list one caller.

name: update_countdown_envelope_level
description: Uses a state byte to decide whether to run a timed level update. When active, it computes a scaled value from two counters and subtracts it from a stored level, then counts down a step counter and handles the end-of-count case.

name: clear_envelope_active_flag
description: Writes zero into one state byte of a structure and returns. The facts list one caller and two unnamed calls, which the pseudo-code does not show.

name: set_field_to_sixty_four
description: Stores sixty-four into a 16-bit field of a structure and returns. The facts list two callers.

name: load_envelope_from_table
description: Reads several bytes from a table entry pointed to by a structure field and copies them into the structure's state fields, then sets the state byte to two. The facts list ten instructions and no callers.

name: reset_envelope_from_table
description: Clears one level byte, negates a stored level into a counter field, copies a table byte into two fields, and sets the state byte to all ones. The facts list one caller.

name: update_position_and_counter
description: Updates an output field from a table-driven scaled value and advances an index with a wrap. While a counter byte is non-zero it adds a step value to an accumulator and decrements the counter, then writes a value through a stored pointer. The facts list one caller.

name: initialize_object_state
description: Sets a value and a zeroed accumulator in a structure, then looks up a table entry and copies its bytes into state fields and a pointer field. The facts list one caller.

name: select_table_entry_when_changed
description: When the requested index byte differs from the one stored, it updates that byte and looks up a 32-byte table entry from a base table. It then copies several words from that entry into the structure. The facts list one caller.

name: return_empty_routine
description: Returns immediately with no effect. The facts list one instruction and an execution in the reference run.

name: open_intuition_and_initialize
description: Opens a library by name, polls one library call until it returns non-zero, then runs several allocation and setup calls. The facts also list an AllocMem and a CloseLibrary call and an empty stub that is called.

name: set_state_four_and_setup
description: Returns early unless the low four bits of a global are zero or eight. Otherwise it sets the global to four and makes four calls to other routines. The facts list one caller and one unnamed call.

name: initialize_state_and_call_routines
description: Runs a sequence of calls, including an empty stub, then copies values between several state globals and a table indexed by a global. It also writes constant words into further state variables. The facts list one caller and four unnamed calls.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Calls one other routine and returns. The facts list one caller and seven instructions, which is more than the single call shown in the pseudo-code.

name: copy_four_planes_then_call
description: Copies eight hundred groups of four words from a source area into four destinations spaced a large fixed distance apart, then calls another routine four times. The facts list one caller.

name: return_empty_routine
description: Returns immediately without doing anything. The facts list one caller and one instruction.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Calls one other routine and returns. The facts list six instructions and show the routine is unreached.

name: store_two_descriptor_records
description: Writes two descriptor records into a structure, each holding a pointer, two words and a flag byte. The first record has its flag set and the second has it cleared.

name: set_mode_two_offsets
description: When a mode variable equals two, sets two word globals to fixed values. When a second global is above a threshold, it replaces them with other fixed values. The facts list one caller.

name: replace_marker_bytes_in_buffer
description: When a mode variable is two or three, scans a large byte buffer and replaces each occurrence of the letter a with a pair of fixed byte values, then clears a global. The facts list one caller.

name: load_mode_indexed_values
description: Uses a mode variable, doubled, to index a word table and a byte table, copying one entry from each into globals. The facts list one caller.

name: run_flagged_wait_sequence
description: When a flag global equals one, makes a call, polls another routine until it returns zero, then sets the flag, makes one more call and clears the flag again. The facts list one caller and one unnamed call.

name: set_state_six_and_halt
description: Sets a global to six, calls one routine, then enters an endless loop that never returns. The facts list one caller.

name: copy_hundred_longs_to_buffer
description: Copies one hundred long words from a fixed global area into a buffer selected through a global pointer. The facts list seven callers.

name: setup_display_and_dma_registers
description: Waits until a global becomes minus one, then writes a series of constants to the display window, fetch, bitplane and copper pointer values, and to the DMA and interrupt enable registers. The facts list two unnamed calls.

name: dispatch_interrupt_request_flags
description: Checks two flag bits in a global. When the first is set it stores a value and returns; when the second is set it stores another value and calls six routines. The facts list the interrupt request register.

name: update_input_status_flags
description: Calls two routines, then sets bit seven of a global variable depending on whether bit six is clear and whether bit seven is clear. The facts list the fire button, mouse and joystick input registers.

name: decode_word_flags_into_byte
description: Clears a byte, then sets its bits from particular bits of a word: two bits derived from an exclusive-or of neighbouring bits, one from a high bit and one from a low bit. The facts list one caller.

name: handshake_keyboard_serial_if_idle
description: When a bit condition on a global holds, runs a keyboard serial handshake. It stores a rotated, inverted copy of a previous status byte, waits for a flag bit, then clears the control registers. The facts list the CIAA interrupt control and INTREQ registers.

name: handshake_keyboard_serial_line
description: Stores a rotated and inverted copy of a previous byte into the keyboard serial register, waits for the serial interrupt flag, then clears the control registers and writes a fixed interrupt control value. The facts also list the CIAA timer registers.

name: copy_long_block_into_buffer
description: Copies a block of sixty-seven long words from a fixed global area into a buffer offset from a global pointer. The facts list one caller.

name: run_row_routines_with_strides
description: Repeatedly calls a called routine with an address and offset that advance by fixed strides per row, repeating each row until the called routine returns zero, then calls two routines. The facts list three unnamed calls.

name: copy_sixteen_rows_from_table
description: Looks up a source block from a table using a byte value, then copies sixteen rows of four words into four destination areas spaced a fixed distance apart. The facts list one caller.

name: lookup_byte_into_destination
description: Reads a byte through a pointer, uses it as an index into a table selected by a global value, and writes the looked-up byte to a destination. The facts list one caller.

name: scan_grid_and_call_cells
description: Walks a grid of cells row by row, calling a called routine for each non-zero table byte, with a stride that advances per row until the row counter wraps. The facts list one unnamed call and that the routine is unreached.

name: fill_sixteen_records_with_ones
description: Writes all ones into the first two long words of sixteen ten-long-word records. The facts list one caller and that the routine is unreached.

name: reset_record_list_flags
description: Walks a list of twelve-word records selected by a mode variable until a sentinel value, clearing one byte in each record and copying another byte into a neighbouring field. The facts list one unnamed call.

name: run_routine_for_each_record
description: Walks a list of records selected by a mode variable and calls a called routine for each one until the sentinel, advancing by a fixed record size. The facts list two unnamed calls and two callers.

name: run_record_in_range_loop
description: When a record's flag is clear and its two coordinates fall inside fixed bounds, runs a loop of routine calls that advances a counter until a status bit is set, then clears state and returns. The facts list one caller and one unnamed call.

name: run_timed_frame_loop
description: Runs an outer loop that resets a frame counter, then repeats a sequence of five routine calls per step, advancing the counter until it reaches a fixed value. A flag bit causes one final call and a return. The facts list four unnamed calls.

name: clear_flag_and_call
description: If a global is non-zero, clears it and calls one other routine. The facts list one caller.

name: run_frame_loop_after_call
description: Calls one routine and then enters the same timed frame loop as the neighbouring entry, which advances a frame counter and makes five calls per step. The facts list two instructions and that the routine is unreached.

name: call_seven_routines_first_frame
description: When the frame counter equals one, calls seven other routines in sequence, and does nothing otherwise. The facts list one caller and one unnamed call.

name: call_routines_at_frame_marker
description: When the frame counter equals a fixed marker value, makes five calls, then one further call and one more. The facts list one caller and one unnamed call.

name: call_routines_at_late_frame
description: When the frame counter reaches a second fixed marker value, calls seven routines. The facts list one caller and one unnamed call.

name: load_mode_table_values
description: Loads a global from a word table indexed by a mode variable, loads another from a pointer table, then calls one other routine. The facts list three callers.

name: check_status_code_and_return
description: Checks a status global against two character codes. One code sets it to one, and when the status equals the second code the routine enters an endless loop. Other values return a result with bits set. The facts list two callers.

name: return_empty_routine
description: Returns immediately with no effect. The facts list one caller and one instruction.

name: poll_routine_until_zero
description: Repeatedly calls one routine until it returns zero, then returns. The facts list six instructions and one unnamed call.

name: advance_row_position_when_aligned
description: When a position value plus six is aligned to a sixteen-step boundary, updates a counter field from a table entry and a flag byte, then sets a routine pointer in the record. The facts list one caller and one unnamed call.

name: fill_arithmetic_sequence_table
description: Fills a table of long words with an arithmetic sequence whose start value comes from a global and whose step is fixed, counting down the number of entries given by another global. The facts list no callers.

name: reset_table_and_load_entry
description: Clears a fixed buffer of 256 bytes, copies four long words from a table entry selected by a global index, then writes a run of fixed constants into a block of globals. The facts list one caller.

name: invert_global_byte
description: Sets a global variable to the bitwise inversion of its low byte. The facts list seven instructions and no callers.

name: call_routine_four_times
description: Calls one other routine four times in a loop and returns. The facts list one caller and one unnamed call.

name: load_channel_slot_with_delay
description: Calls one routine, then loads a pointer and a word from a table entry and stores them into per-channel slots. When a flag byte is set it waits in a short delay loop and stores a fixed value and pointer. The facts list the DMA control register and three unnamed calls.

name: store_word_at_channel_offset
description: Stores the incoming word through a pointer computed from a structure base and an index. The facts list three callers.

name: store_scaled_byte_at_offset
description: Stores the low byte of an input word, shifted left by two, into a word slot at a computed offset. The facts list two callers.

name: call_two_routines_in_order
description: Calls two other routines and returns. The facts list five instructions and that the routine is unreached.

name: advance_channel_sequence_state
description: Updates the state of one per-channel structure. It returns early when a flag is set, otherwise it counts down a timer byte and, when the timer reaches zero, reloads it and advances a pointer through a sequence. The facts list the DMA control register, thirteen callers and three unnamed calls.

name: apply_channel_value_byte
